THE BIFOLIUM — one A4 landscape sheet, folded once.

Print side A:  face 4 | face 1
Print side B:  face 2 | face 3

So the fact panel is the back cover and the letter's close is the inside-right.

Each face is A5 trim 148 x 210 mm on a 154 x 216 mm canvas — the extra 3 mm all round is bleed. Dashed red is the trim; dashed teal is the 12 mm margin. Both switch off with the Guides chip above each artboard before you export.

THIS ONE DOES NOT FIT, AND THE ARTBOARD SHOWS IT.

The fact panel is drawn at 16 px — 12 pt, the print floor — and it runs about 190 px (50 mm) past the bottom of the A5 sheet. The red line marks where the sheet ends; everything on the grey below it is off the paper.

This is a new finding. Moving the letter to A4-folded fixed the letter and did not fix the panel: faces 1-3 now have slack and face 4 has none.

Three ways out, all of them your call:
  1. Panel takes faces 3 and 4 as a spread, letter takes 1-2.
  2. Trim the six bullets — but they are the spec.
  3. Drop the panel to about 10.5 pt, under the print floor.

Nothing here decides it. The panel is drawn to the skeleton in fact-panel-spec.md so you can see the real size of the problem.

THE A6 CARDS — 105 x 148 mm trim on a 111 x 154 mm canvas, 8 mm margin.

Hadith card: the saying IS selected (Tuhaf al-Uqul, maxim 112, trans. Badr Shahin) and is set exactly as published. The SEGMENT NUMBER is not — this file's draft calls the Prophet segment 1 and spec-check.md calls him 13, and two cards currently claim segment 1. The card prints a marked blank until that is decided.

The chain mark is written out in words — 'Silsila segment n of 14' — because the companions line's 'First Edition nn / 39' sits in the same corner at the same size, and a child sorts two bare numbers into one pile.

No envelope number appears anywhere on either face. That is the rule most likely to leak from a template copied off the fact panel.

POSTCARD, FLAP, ENVELOPE.

The envelope is C5, 229 x 162 mm — it has to take an A5 stack now that the letter folds from A4. That size follows from the fold decision; it was not fixed before.

The cancellation mark is drawn as real SVG, so it scales and recolours: gold ring on standard issues, charcoal on 01 and 02. Killer bars to the right, month around the ring, envelope number in the centre.

The postcard's return address is bracketed, not invented.

The flap is sized to a 148 x 100 mm working area. Re-size it once the envelope is actually chosen.

NOT DRAWN HERE, AND DELIBERATELY.

Person print, event print, sticker sheet and the postcard front are illustration, not typesetting. They need an illustrator and, for the event print, a physically proofed ring punch first.

Also still true:
  - Every claim on the fact panel is TO VERIFY. The watermark stays until its rows read V.
  - The source credit is bracketed because the Guillaume citation was removed under the Shia-sources-only rule and nothing has replaced it.
  - Nothing here has been read aloud to a child or timed.
